articles.title: Reading 1-2 Brentford: Bees book place in Carabao Cup fourth round with tense win at League One side
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup third round tie between Reading and Brentford at the Select Car Leasing Stadium; Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half for the Premier League club; Paudie O’Connor gave League One side hope of comeback
articles.body:
Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho were on target in the first half as the Premier League club showed a clinical touch against League One opposition, who produced a number of chances but lacked the firepower to finish them off.

Paudie O'Connor eventually pulled one back to revive Reading's challenge and Brentford could not rest easy in the remaining 18 minutes, although substitute Igor Thiago was among those who should have killed the match off.

It took just 136 seconds for Brentford to take the lead with Wilson finding the bottom left corner of the net after a slip in defence by O'Connor turned Dango Ouattara's pass into an opportunity.

A cross by Carvalho caused problems in the visiting box and Reading then had the ball in the net but referee Tom Nield ruled out O'Connor's bicycle kick for a high boot.

O'Connor was doing everything possible to make up for his earlier mistake as he headed a free-kick inches over the crossbar.

Reading had clearly recovered from the shock of going behind so early as they poured forward, with a double clearance by Michael Kayode saving Brentford before Jamie Reid went desperately close.

O'Connor slipped again as he fluffed a clearance, giving Wilson time to pick his spot only for keeper Joel Pereira to get his body in the way.

Brentford scrambled to keep out Reid as he closed in on goal and then Conor Masterson flashed narrowly wide, but the Premier League club then scored on the counter-attack.

In a cruel blow for the Royals, Ouattara took advantage of the space in defence to slide the ball to Carvalho who calmly directed the ball beyond Pereira.

Ellery Balcombe's sharp reflexes prevented Josh Stokes from pulling one back for Reading but Brentford should have extended the lead only for Kayode to send a close-range effort wide.

Liam Fraser reminded the visitors they could not relax as he drilled a shot past the left post but the better chances were now coming at the other end, with Ouattara this time at fault for not making the most of a great opportunity.

Reading deserved a goal and it arrived in the 72nd minute when a corner was met by O'Connor's header, with the Irish defender's finish setting up a nervy finale.

On came Thiago but he was unable to improve the standard of finishing by his team, which had declined noticeably in the second half.

articles.title: Texas QB Arch Manning should know better, but it's hard to blame just him for viral moment when his whole life has been scripted
articles.summary: Saturday was Texas' biggest win in years, and the Longhorns certainly deserve all the praise for coming back from a 23-3 deficit in the fourth quarter to win...
articles.body:
Holly Rowe has been the most prominent female sideline reporter on ESPN's college football telecasts for a couple decades, which means we only know about a small percentage of the sexist garbage she has to deal with on a daily basis.

But we should all be able to understand, even for a seasoned pro like Rowe, the awfulness of the challenge she now faces. Every time ESPN's top broadcast team is assigned to the Texas Longhorns , she will know that the most prominent player on the team — and very likely many of his teammates — were in the locker room yucking it up over an AI-generated video of head coach Steve Sarkisian slapping her.

As thrilling as Texas' 24-23 comeback victory over Ohio State was on Saturday night , the aftermath has been an embarrassing, toxic mess.

On Sunday, you had a candidate for statewide office — a Republican named Bo French — ruining a picture of the postgame celebration that showed the joy of some Texas students by twisting it into racist grievance because of their skin color. It blew up into a social media debacle, drawing condemnation from many in his own party and elevating a race for Texas railroad commissioner into a national story.

Then on Monday, Texas quarterback Arch Manning strode in for his weekly press conference, which was going well enough until someone asked him if he had seen any "edits" on social media of the postgame scene.

"I've seen a few AI edits of stuff, but that's about it," Manning said, starting off innocently enough. "I saw an AI edit of Sark's interview. (Laughter in the room.) Y'all seen that one? That's a good one … of him slapping Holly Rowe. (More laughter.) It's hilarious."

Though it took 24 hours, credit to Manning for issuing an apology Tuesday : "In my press conference yesterday, I made an insensitive comment about an AI video. There is nothing funny about it. It's easy to say I didn't mean it, but I know my words and actions were hurtful to a lot of people. I do not take that lightly and am deeply sorry for that.

"I specifically want to apologize to Holly Rowe for what she has personally had to deal with because of my comments. I have a ton of respect for her and appreciate her showing me grace in this moment. I need to do better and will be more thoughtful going forward."

It was a necessary clean-up job, but the work isn't done.

Because we would not be here if Sarkisian simply acted like a normal human being Saturday night. Though he was understandably frustrated when he had to bail on the standard halftime interview due to technical issues on ESPN's end, there was no reason for Sarkisian to bigfoot Rowe in the postgame scramble by yelling "Texas Fight, Hook 'em!" and then storming off rather than standing there for 30 seconds and answering two questions like every winning coach does after every game.

Sure, these interviews don't add a ton to the broadcast because you're not usually getting deep insights into the game amidst the adrenaline rush of victory. But the way Sarkisian acted was disrespectful and immature — and it obviously trickled down to Texas fans on the internet and his locker room.

You can't do much about somebody taking the video of that interview and using AI to invent a new ending where Sarkisian turns toward Rowe, knocks her to the ground with the back of his hand and runs off with fists raised. The internet is going to do what the internet's going to do.

But it's not funny. A man hitting a woman, real or AI-generated, should never be turned into entertainment.

Manning is a college student, but he is also a 22-year-old grown man who was surely raised to understand that violence against women — even if it comes in the form of satire — is inappropriate. He's also, as we saw Monday, still a bit of an immature kid who's got some growing up to do and his apology was a good first step.

We're not here to "cancel" Manning or call for him to be suspended or lose his endorsements.

And it's understood that since 2024, a segment of America that tends to be very loud on social media has launched a cultural backlash against the policing of offensive speech. But it's not reasonable to see violence against women, even if intended to be comedy, as a place to draw the line.

For a player who has lived much of his life in the spotlight and been pretty buttoned-up in his public comments, it was a surprising whiff by Manning and a moment that he'll hopefully learn the right lesson from.

Teams take on the personality of their coach, and Sarkisian has had other incidents during his time at Texas where he raged at folks who are just trying to do their job. Remember the Alamo Bowl in 2022 when he screamed obscenities at a staff member in the tunnel who was trying to get him to wait before running on the field?

If he's that comfortable being a jerk to people when the cameras are on, it makes you wonder what he's like behind the scenes when something doesn't go exactly how he wants it.

For anyone who has been around college football teams, with all that testosterone flowing through the locker room and a culture of trying to out-bro each other, it's not a huge surprise that players would find their coach belittling a sideline reporter kind of funny. And anyone who has spent time around Gen Z knows how influenced they are by absurdity on social media.

But if you want your program to be about turning boys into good men, you should set that example in how you interact with women on national television. Rowe is too professional and too good to be turned into the butt of a joke in the Texas locker room. There is nothing cool or funny about an image of her on the ground as a victim of a violent slap, even if it's fake.

Saturday was Texas' biggest victory in years, and the Longhorns certainly deserve all the praise for coming back from a 23-3 deficit in the fourth quarter to win.

But within 72 hours, nobody was talking about that anymore. Instead, a racist tweet by a politician and a cringeworthy media appearance by Texas' star quarterback was consuming all the oxygen.

Texas looked like a potential national championship team on Saturday. By Monday night, it looked like a program that isn't ready for prime time.

As a young guy figuring all this out, Manning deserves a little bit of grace. But the fundamental issue that led him to it — including the fawning Texas media laughing it up with him — is an organizational problem.

Maybe Sarkisian doesn't care. But he's not serving himself, his players or his university very well by opening the door for a standard postgame interview to become a sexist meme.

articles.title: Lionel Messi called up by Argentina for farewell match on Oct. 6 in Buenos Aires
articles.summary: Messi announced on Aug. 31 he was retiring from Argentina's national team after leading them to three World Cup finals.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi will take part in a farewell match with Argentina on Oct. 6 against Benin in Buenos Aires as part of the upcoming international break.

The 39-year-old Messi announced on Aug. 31 that he was retiring from national team duties saying in a social media message, "I've given everything I had; I have nothing left to give, and besides, there are some great young players coming up who deserve to be here."

Argentina is set to face Bolivia at Estadio Mario Alberto Kempes in Córdoba on Sept. 30. They will also play Burkina Faso on Oct. 3 and Benin on Oct. 6 with the final two matches taking place at Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires during the extended FIFA international window.

Estadio Monumental's capacity of 85,018 makes it the largest stadium in South America.

Messi's farewell message came weeks after Argentina lost to Spain in the World Cup final , which saw the soccer legend walk off the MetLife Stadium field holding back tears.

Nearly a month later, Messi's father, Jorge, died after dealing with an undisclosed illness at age 68.

Messi has scored 125 goals in 207 appearances with Argentina. He led the Albiceleste to two Copa América titles in 2021 and 2024, as well as three World Cup finals, including 2022 when Argentina beat France.

Following the 2026 World Cup, Messi returned to his club team, Inter Miami , which is second in the Eastern Conference. Through 22 games, he leads the league with 19 goals and 32 goal contributions.

articles.title: A high school football rule was intended to reduce head injuries. Researchers have discovered a totally different benefit
articles.summary: There are an estimated 100,000-150,000 concussion cases linked to high school football each year
articles.body:
A high school football rule, introduced 12 years ago to reduce serious head injuries among players , has had an unintended benefit: fewer leg injuries .

The nationwide rule banned American football players from hitting opponents above their shoulders, in an effort to protect their heads. Head impacts in football have become an increasing concern for players and their families because of recent studies tying head injuries to CTE, a progressive brain disorder that raises the risk of dementia .

But new research shows that the high school rule is having an impact in an unexpected way. Emergency room data showed there were decreased numbers of lower body injuries among high school players.

The researchers were surprised because they had feared lower body injuries would increase with the regulation that reduces tackles to the upper body.

"We were just thinking as people are avoiding the head and neck, they're going to be tackling lower in the body, so maybe the injury burden might be getting shifted lower in the body," Nolan Tanji, a University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa's John A. Burns School of Medicine student, said in a statement .

However, it was not all good news - there were more collisions between players after the rule than there were before.

The researchers hope further data will be able to shed light on why that's the case.

Tanji and his classmates examined more than 14,000 ER entries of athletes aged 14-18 from five years before the rule's implementation and five years after it took effect.

The data showed that there was a yearly average of 7,315 lower-extremity injury cases before the rule and only 5,611 afterward.

Using those cases to estimate the same drop nationwide, the researchers said these injuries plummeted from an average of 242,000 before the rule to 193,000 injuries after the rule.

There were also fewer knee injuries after the rule took effect.

"It's not completely safe but, you know, it's looking promising for the future in terms of injuries in football," Tanji noted.

The findings suggest that the rule is more beneficial than previously believed and there has been a decrease in neck injuries since 2014, separate research uncovered in 2022.

However, the researchers say that the rule cannot necessarily be credited for causing the decline.

Changes in training, injury prevention and equipment technology may have all played a role, the researchers suggest.

And the database also only included injuries treated in emergency departments and there was no way of knowing which positions the injured athletes played.

Running backs that rush the ball and linemen that protect the quarterback are the most likely to receive hits, 2011 research from Brown University found.

Football is one of the top sports for head injuries, federal data shows, with tackling responsible for 63 percent of concussions.

There are an estimated 100,000-150,000 concussion cases linked to high school football each year, according to the Athletic Equipment Managers Association , though around half of all concussions are unreported.

Repeated concussions can lead to CTE, also known as chronic traumatic encephalopathy, Boston University researchers say.

articles.title: Tottenham's misery continues with loss at Liverpool in English League Cup. Arsenal cruises to win
articles.summary: As for big-spending Tottenham, just scoring a goal is a feat in itself this season.  The current gulf between the two north London rivals was highlighted in...
articles.body:
Arsenal can't stop winning. As for big-spending Tottenham , just scoring a goal is a feat in itself this season.

The current gulf between the two north London rivals was highlighted in the English League Cup on Tuesday, with Arsenal fielding almost an entire second-choice lineup and still overwhelming fellow Premier League team Ipswich in a 4-2 win in the third round.

Max Dowman , a 16-year-old prodigy, enhanced his budding reputation with a goal early in each half, while Noni Madueke and Mikel Merino also netted for the English champions as they soared into a 4-0 lead.

It was a sixth straight win across all competitions to open the season for Arsenal, which is showing impressive strength in depth that should enable Mikel Arteta's squad to challenge on multiple fronts.

Then there's Tottenham, which isn't getting much return on its incredible $400 million outlay on new players in the summer transfer window.

A 3-1 loss in the pouring rain at Liverpool means Spurs' only victory in six games this season was against second-tier Charlton in the previous round of the League Cup.

They have played four matches in the Premier League — drawing two and losing two — and have yet to score a single goal.

Conor Gallagher 's header at a corner in the 69th minute gave Tottenham hope after goals by Alexis Mac Allister and Cody Gakpo put Liverpool 2-0 ahead. Dominik Szoboszlai 's long-range piledriver in the first minute of stoppage time ended any chance of a comeback.

Tottenham isn't playing in European competition this season, so its only realistic chance of silverware lies with the FA Cup starting in January.

Premier League teams Fulham and Brentford also advanced to the fourth round Tuesday.

Fulham won 3-2 at second-tier West Ham and Brentford beat third-tier Reading 2-1.

There will be more third-round games on Wednesday and Thursday.

articles.title: Liverpool pile on misery for Spurs in League Cup, Dowman dazzles for Arsenal
articles.summary: Liverpool piled on the misery for troubled Tottenham with a 3-1 win in the League Cup third round, while teenage star Max Dowman dazzled for Arsenal in their...
articles.body:
Liverpool piled on the misery for troubled Tottenham with a 3-1 win in the League Cup third round, while teenage star Max Dowman dazzled for Arsenal in their 4-2 rout of Ipswich on Tuesday.

After a woeful start to the Premier League season, Tottenham's hopes of a morale-boosting cup run came to a dispiriting end at rain-lashed Anfield.

They were swatted aside by Liverpool, with Alexis Mac Allister , Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai scoring for the Reds.

Roberto De Zerbi's fourth-bottom team are without a win or even a goal in their first four league matches, losing twice and drawing twice.

Tottenham's only win this season has come in the League Cup against second-tier Charlton.

After successive 17th place finishes -- including avoiding relegation on the final day of last season -- the north London club spent over £300 million ($404 million) on 10 new signings since the end of last term.

But the return on that eye-watering investment has not been immediate, sparking fears of another relegation battle.

Adding to De Zerbi's problems, unsettled striker Richarlison took to social media to lament the Italian's decision to leave him out of the squad to face Liverpool.

Richarlison wants to leave but moves to Everton and Vasco Da Gama have fallen through recently.

Tottenham host Aston Villa on Saturday in a game that De Zerbi desperately needs to win to ease the pressure on him going into the international break.

Liverpool remain unbeaten at the start of the Andoni Iraola era, although they have won just once in four league matches.

Iraola made 10 changes but Liverpool went ahead after 21 minutes with a flowing move.

Gakpo picked out Rio Ngumoha and he teed up Mac Allister to blast a first-time finish past Martin Dubravka into the roof of the net.

Gakpo doubled Liverpool's advantage in the 54th minute, whipping a fine strike into the far corner.

Tottenham finally scored a goal against top-flight opposition this season -- albeit in a different competition -- when Conor Gallagher punished poor marking to net from a corner in the 69th minute.

But Szoboszlai rubbed salt into Tottenham's wounds in stoppage-time with a 25-yard rocket.

At Portman Road, Dowman took centre stage to remember Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta of his burgeoning talent.

Arsenal, who lost the League Cup final against Manchester City last season, have won their six games in all competitions this term.

Arteta made nine changes from the side that won at Sunderland on Saturday, with 16-year-old Dowman given his first appearance this season.

Dowman has been ear-marked as a future star since bursting onto the scene as a 15-year-old last season.

But Arteta is treating the midfielder with kid gloves, bringing him on slowly while the Premier League champions are thriving.

Dowman showed Arteta what he can add to the party in the seventh minute, flashing quick feet to skip past Cedric Kipre before slotting home with a composed finish.

It was Dowman's second goal for Arsenal after his strike against Everton in March.

Noni Madueke increased Arsenal's lead in the 16th minute, lashing a low shot past Christian Walton from just inside the penalty area.

Dowman struck again in the 47th minute, running onto Martin Zubimendi 's pass and finishing with aplomb.

Mikel Merino grabbed Arsenal's fourth, curling home from Dowman's pass in the 58th minute.

Anis Mehmeti 's 62nd minute reply and Chuba Akpom 's stoppage-time strike were little consolation for out-classed Ipswich.

Fulham made nine changes but still won 3-2 at Championship leaders West Ham , with goals from Rodrigo Muniz , Cesar Palacios and Oscar Bobb , who bagged the 78th minute winner.

Brentford won 2-1 at third tier Reading thanks to goals from Callum Wilson and Fabio Carvalho .

On Wednesday, Manchester United host Brighton , Aston Villa travel to Coventry and Everton face Wolves.

Holders Manchester City are at home to Norwich on Thursday.

articles.title: La agresión de Osorio a Huijsen merecía más repeticiones
articles.standfirst: La contracrónica del Elche - Real Madrid
articles.summary: La contracrónica del Elche - Real Madrid
articles.body: Nos hemos acostumbrado en el fútbol actual a que haya jugadas que necesiten cinco repeticiones, tres líneas, un máster en geometría y una reunión de expertos para decidir si es legal o no. Lo aceptamos ya como parte del juego. Lo que cuesta más aceptar es que las acciones que se ven, o se deberían ver, a la primera, como la agresión de Osorio a Huijsen, no se penalicen. No tiene justificación lo que sucedió en Elche. Fue un codazo tremendo y deliberado, de roja directa, que pasó casi de puntillas por el partido porque apenas se repitió y porque para los árbitros fue un lance del juego. Gil Manzano no lo vio sobre el césped y, más sorprendente todavía, nadie desde el VAR (Martín González) consideró oportuno invitarle a echar un vistazo al monitor. Debían estar con otra cosa. La acción, insistimos, solo se repitió una vez, pero fue suficiente para no dejar demasiado espacio para el debate. Osorio agredió a Huijsen y debía haberse marchado a la calle. Mourinho sí lo vio desde el banquillo y protestó con insistencia al cuarto árbitro, pero como el que oye llover. Mou, esta vez, tenía motivos de sobra para quejarse. Lo increíble es que, con un ejército de cámaras y una sala dedicada precisamente a detectar lo que se le escapa al árbitro, la jugada terminara como si nada hubiera pasado. Ni roja, ni revisión, ni monitor. Sigan, sigan... Y Osorio encontró el gol en la segunda parte. Y dicho esto: luego está lo del Madrid. Lo de sus siestas, sus desconexiones, la falta de puntería de Vini, el cambio de Güler... Estar a punto de dejarse dos puntos en Elche tras ir ganando a 0-2 tiene delito... En el minuto 33, Diomande recibió un balón en profundidad de Fede Valverde y aprovechó para hacerle un regalo a Mbappé. Una asistencia perfecta. O mejor que eso. La jugada que necesitaba el extremo para hacer click. Diomande, que celebró el pase como si fuera su primer gol con la camiseta del Real Madrid, fue otro desde esa acción. Más incisivo, más vertical, más valiente... el de Costa de Marfil empezó a mostrar de verdad parte de su repertorio. Diomande se liberó y dejó muy buenas sensaciones por hacer también cosas que muchos extremos han dejado de hacer: atacar el espacio y defender. Dos acciones básicas que, por ejemplo, cada vez se ven menos en Vinicius. En definitiva, un gran partido que quizás le sirva para despegar. Pocos dudaban de que la falta de Güler en la frontal acabaría en gol. El turco tiene posiblemente el mejor guante de LaLiga y adelantó al Madrid con un golazo de libre directo con el que dejó a Dituro haciendo la estatua. La zurda de oro siempre la tuvo, pero ahora tiene la personalidad para coger la pelota y monopolizar todas las acciones a balón parado. Nadie en el Madrid le pega a la pelota como él. El gol fue la guinda de otro partido en el que dejó mil detalles y se confirmó, una vez más, como el faro del equipo blanco. Curiosamente, fue marcharse del campo y empezar a ganar metros el Elche... Lo dijo Mou en la previa. "A Vini le falta el gol para tener una alta performance". Pues ante el Elche tampoco. El brasileño estuvo negado todo el partido y falló un par de ocasiones claras en las que quedó clara su ansiedad de cara a puerta. En la primera parte, solo ante Dituro, definió con la puntera y mandó el balón muy lejos del marco. En la segunda, a pase de Arda, mandó el balón al lateral de la red. Una mala noche, llena de imprecisiones, que acabó con Mou sustituyéndole para que cogiera aire de cara al derbi. Le pasó ante el Rayo y le volvió a pasar ante el Elche. Tras una buena primera parte, el Madrid bajó los brazos. El problema en esta ocasión es que el marcador era 0-2, no 3-0 como en el Bernabéu. El Madrid dejó que el Elche se metiera en el partido y se llevó un susto de los buenos en vísperas del derbi. Espí vuelve a salir en la foto de la victoria, pero esta vez fueron Bellingham y Mbappé los que arreglaron el desaguisado. Mourinho ya tiene a su cinco. Tchouaméni disputó su primer partido como titular y ofreció un nivel físico lo suficientemente bueno como para dar su lesión por olvidada. Directo al once del derbi. Jugó al lado de Fede Valverde, que va a ser su pareja en buena parte de los partidos de esta temporada. Un doble pivote que, eso sí, va a necesitar mucha ayuda de Güler para sacar la pelota con claridad...

articles.title: Motherwell 0-4 Aberdeen: Dons secure first league win since opening day in emphatic style at Fir Park
articles.summary: Report as Aberdeen beat Motherwell 4-0 in the William Hill Scottish Premiership
articles.body:
Gavin Molloy put Stephen Robinson's side ahead shortly before half-time, before Connor Ronan put some daylight between the sides just seconds after the restart.

Motherwell huffed and puffed without troubling the Dons' rearguard, and the visitors put some gloss on the scoreline late on courtesy of strikes from Ayoub Mouloua and Kevin Nisbet.

The win - Aberdeen's first in the William Hill Premiership since the opening day - moved the men from the Granite City to within a point of fifth-placed Motherwell with one game to come before the international break.

The hosts made just one change from their defeat against Rangers at Ibrox 10 days ago, with Jardell Kanga coming in for Ibrahim Said.

Dons boss Stephen Robinson made three following their penalty shootout triumph over Kilmarnock in the Premier Sports Cup quarter-final on Saturday, as Molloy, Toyusi Olusanya and Findlay Marshall came in for Dan Happe, Mitchy Ntelo and Stuart Armstrong.

Having spent the first 10 minutes on the back foot, Aberdeen finally came to life when Afeez Aremu took aim from range, only to see his powerful volley fall just wide with Alex Paulsen scrambling.

Motherwell dominated the opening half hour but lacked a cutting edge in the final third, with an Emmanuel Longelo strike from a tight angle - comfortably parried away by Marius Muller - the best they could muster.

Marshall and Nisbet both saw curling strikes from range narrowly miss the target before Molloy showed them how it is done by drilling a piledriver into the bottom corner after Motherwell failed to clear their lines in the 38th minute.

Ronan doubled the Dons' advantage within 30 seconds of the restart, capitalising on slack play out from the back to beat Paulsen from 20 yards with the aid of a deflection.

Substitute Seb Palmer-Houlden should have done better with a header from six yards, and Motherwell were made to pay for that miss when Mouloua put the outcome beyond doubt with 15 minutes to play.

Nisbet did well to feed Ronan midway inside his own half, and the midfielder played a wonderful through ball into the Moroccan's path.

A poor touch initially looked to have taken the chance away from him, but he regrouped and rifled high into the roof of the net to send the small band of travelling supporters behind the goal wild.

And it got even better with three minutes to play when Nisbet outmuscled his marker and slid home after latching on to a hopeful ball over the top to seal a first league win on the road this calendar year.

"They're a really good team and to put in that level of performance and score so many goals…not many do it here.

"It was a very good performance after a really gutsy cup win. It gives some momentum but it's a few games and we need to continue to do it. It's my job to ignore the noise. It's not going to be straightforward so I have to keep the players believing.

"Winning gives you belief. You could see them growing into the game with the times they broke, it could have been more.

"We had a lot of penetration and we've not had an end product but tonight we did, so I'm very happy.

"The players deserve the credit, not me. It's easy to coach, but they're the ones who have to do it after the shift with 10 men on Saturday and they did it to the letter."

We played a good first half. There are things to adjust to be even more dangerous. We had really good scenarios in the first half where we're normally really good.

"They go into half-time leading 1-0, it's not perfect but if we adjust our attacking phases and find our players in their best positions, we'd try to go and win the game.

"After 30 seconds we conceded after build-up phase and that's a punch in the face. I didn't like the reaction.

"We stress, and it's so difficult emotionally for a young team to keep their cool and stay on track, and in that moment we lost the structure a bit."

articles.title: Hibernian 0-1 Kilmarnock: Pressure mounting on David Gray as visitors pick up their first win of the season
articles.summary: Report as Kilmarnock beat Hibernian 1-0 in the William Hill Scottish Premiership; pressure mounting on David Gray as Hibs fans boo the team at the full-time whistle
articles.body:
The defender bundled in a loose ball five minutes before the break to give the visitors their first three points of the season.

Killie should have added to their lead in a lively second half before then having to fend off intense late pressure.

The Hibs fans booed their team off as the pressure on head coach David Gray intensified.

Gray made just one change to the team that overcame Ross County 3-0 in the Premier Sports Cup on Saturday - Jacob Devaney coming in for club captain Joe Newell.

Kilmarnock's own cup journey came to an end in a bitterly disappointing shoot-out defeat to 10-man Aberdeen and boss Neil McCann freshened up his side.

Bailey Rice - on loan from Rangers - was handed a first start in the middle of the park while MJ Kamson-Kamara - on a temporary deal from Hearts - was given his debut in defence.

Hibs started brightly and created a good opening after just four minutes.

Felix Passlack found Thibault Klidje and the striker laid it off to Josh Mulligan. The midfielder moved the ball onto his left but his attempt to find the top corner was well off target.

The home team were then forced into a change after just eight minutes when Kanayo Megwa hobbled off and was replaced by Grant Hanley.

The first half became a scrappy affair with neither side able to get a foothold.

Killie fashioned a couple of half chances that fell to Tyreece John-Jules but the towering striker was unable to capitalise.

But the away side took the lead five minutes before the break through Stanger.

Erik Ring's cross into the area was heading for goal and goalkeeper Rafa Sallinger had to be alert to make the block.

But the danger wasn't cleared and Stanger bundled the loose ball in from eight yards.

Killie had their tails up at the start of the second half and Hibs struggled to regain their composure as the groans from the home fans grew louder.

Rice had a powerful free-kick pushed away by Sallinger before the Hibs goalkeeper then kept out Greg Kiltie from a tight angle.

Joe Hugill thought he had doubled his team's lead in the 56th minute after getting on the end of Ring's low cross into the six-yard box.

But their celebrations were cut short after the VAR ruled that there had been an offside in the build-up.

That gave Hibs a boost after substitute Miguel Chaiwa had a stinging drive from 18 yards pushed over by Max Stryjek as they chased a leveller.

Hibs continued to live dangerously and Hugill wasted further chances.

The forward fired into the side netting from a counter-attack led by Ring and then had a shot blocked by Sallinger when he only had the keeper to beat from eight yards.

Hibs piled on the pressure late on but struggled to create any meaningful openings.

Defender Jason Kerr twice got headers away but goalkeeper Stryjek made a comfortable save before seeing the other drift wide.

Killie also had to contend with Djenairo Daniels picking up a second yellow card in the dying moments.

"I've been here during difficult times and I've been here during good times and you can't just say it's brilliant when things are going well and then not expect a bit of criticism when things aren't.

"In terms of asking for patience, the fans are frustrated because we're not achieving what we need to be at this stage and winning enough games consistently, especially at home.

"And I accept that. All I can say is until someone tells me otherwise I will be doing everything in my power, everything I possibly can as I have done at this football club to turn it around and I believe we can.

"It's a difficult time for everybody, the players, football club because we've lost again off the back of a good result at the weekend and then failed to back it up again."

"I don't think I can ask anything more of that team down there - proper unity, proper togetherness and a proper will to see that out.

"We were asked some serious big questions about character.

"We had a goal chopped off, a stonewall penalty on Joe (Hugill) and big Rafa Sallinger had some brilliant saves.

"As a group of players that have just lost a penalty shootout for a chance to go to Hampden and missing out on that, psychologically that's a big test.

"But my God they come through it with flying colours. The keeper made some brilliant saves. I think you've just got to compliment the keeper on making big saves at that time.

"At the end we're soaking up pressure and Hibs are going to load it on you because of their shape and they're going to ask questions.

"We stood up to that and still had that threat ourselves going forward, we turned into a really good counter-attacking team.

"We had some big chances to put ourselves clear but it's a really good three points."

articles.title: Peterborough 3-3 Barnsley (7-6 on pens): Posh edge Carabao Cup third-round tie on penalties
articles.summary: Report and free match highlights from the Carabao Cup third round tie between Peterborough and Barnsley at the Weston Homes Stadium; Posh beat visitors 7-6 on penalties after six-goal thriller; Peterborough move into the fourth round of the Carabao Cup for the first time since 2009
articles.body:
Barnsley were gifted the lead after 61 seconds when Peterborough goalkeeper Alex Bass was charged down by Cameron McGeehan, with the Tykes captain nodding in after the ball had come off the bar.

Peterborough equalised in the 19th minute when Lucca Mendonca's cross was pushed out by Barnsley goalkeeper Kieran Flavell as far as Harry Leonard, who prodded in.

The hosts then completed the turnaround after 27 minutes when Harley Mills' free-kick was headed in by the unmarked Danny Ormerod.

But the Tykes were level five minutes before half-time when Reyes Cleary beat Mendonca with ease down the left before placing his shot into the bottom corner.

The visitors looked to have won it when Cleary bent in his second in the 74th minute, but Ormerod sent the tie to penalties by heading in Mills' cross with just two minutes remaining.

After 12 successful spot-kicks, a tame effort from Barnsley's Luke Alker was saved by Bass, giving Harrison Jones the chance to send the hosts through, which he dispatched.

articles.title: Falkirk 2-1 Hearts: Owen Eames' winner hands hosts first league win of the season
articles.summary: Report as Falkirk beat Hearts 2-1 in the William Hill Scottish Premiership; Owen Eames scored the winning goal of the game as Wouter Vrancken rued his side's poor performance
articles.body:
The on-loan Derby teenager capitalised on a mistake from Jambos captain Harry Milne in the 68th minute to earn the Bairns a 2-1 victory at Falkirk Stadium after James Wilson had cancelled out Ben Krauhaus's early opener for the hosts.

While the Bairns savoured their first league win at the sixth attempt, it was a frustrating night for the off-colour Jambos, who were hoping to climb into second place after winning each of their previous six domestic matches.

Falkirk boss John McGlynn selected the same side that started the 1-1 draw at Dundee United.

Amid a spate of midfield injuries, Wouter Vrancken handed Yan Dhanda his first Hearts start in 16 months. Attackers Josh McPake and Wilson - both included in the Scotland squad earlier in the day - were among those restored after being rotated for Friday's Premier Sports Cup win at Stenhousemuir.

Referee John Beaton - officiating his first Hearts match since contentiously awarding title rivals Celtic a crucial penalty against Motherwell in May - was baited by the Jambos support as he led the teams out the tunnel and he found himself reaching for his yellow card with just over two minutes on the clock to caution Falkirk midfielder Finley Barbrook for a foul on Dhanda.

The Bairns made the breakthrough in the eighth minute when captain Brad Spencer sprayed a pass out to the right, allowing Ryan Strain to ghost in behind the Hearts defence and cut the ball back for Krauhaus, who fired home from 10 yards out.

Hearts, having previously offered little in attack, drew level from their first chance of the match in the 22nd minute when McPake skinned Strain on the left of the penalty box and slid an inviting low delivery across goal for Wilson, who was perfectly placed for a close-range tap-in.

A little over a minute later, the same two players combined once more but Wilson blazed over from 15 yards out.

Falkirk had a great chance to restore their lead on the half hour when Eames got himself clear in the Hearts box but opted to square it instead of shooting and Stuart Findlay scrambled the ball behind.

Hearts sent on JJ Williams in place of Wilson for the start of the second half. The Bairns had another big opportunity four minutes after the break but Barbrook was denied by Beau Reus after Jacob Murrell teed him up in a central position 12 yards out.

At the other end, Williams and Calvin Miller both saw close-range efforts saved by Scott Bain, who was also included in the Scotland squad.

Eames and Murrell then spurned big chances for the hosts before they restored their lead in the 68th minute.

Milne played a risky pass from the left-back position towards centre-back Jamie McCart and it was intercepted by Eames, who drove forward and fired a low shot in off Reus's right-hand post from just inside the box.

"Poor performance, simple. How we started the game, with miscommunication, not enough concentration, too easy in the back and then we were too slow to get back into our organisation, it was not good enough.

"I saw some panic in the team actually in the first half. We were too reactive and not proactive and when you're not proactive in situations, then you don't show solutions and so then you cannot dominate the game.

"Second half when we came out were a bit better. Also we wanted with JJ someone who holds the ball a bit more so that we could also do maybe something more offensively and at the beginning it worked with a big chance for JJ.

"It could have changed things there if he finished it because then you go ahead. But at the end it was just not good enough and it was a deserved victory for Falkirk.

"The team effort was not enough, too many players under their level. We had some moments in the game but we had no reason to think the game could be ours today."

"It was good to get the monkey off our back," he said. "The fixture list wasn't kind to us but I'm delighted for the players tonight.

"You have to work so hard to win any game in this league and they did that. We got out the blocks well and scored a good goal.

"It's hard to stop a team like Hearts coming back into the game but we should have done better at their equaliser.

"We took over after Scott Bain saved from Williams in the second half. We had good chances and deserved the win overall. It gives us a huge lift."

articles.title: Espí vuelve a evitar un desastre
articles.standfirst: El tanto del ariete en el 91' da el triunfo a un Madrid que se pone 0-2 en un buen primer tiempo y se desconecta tras el descanso. Osorio y Fer Niño empatan para un Elche que cede al final
articles.summary: El tanto del ariete en el 91' da el triunfo a un Madrid que se pone 0-2 en un buen primer tiempo y se desconecta tras el descanso. Osorio y Fer Niño empatan para un Elche que cede al final
articles.body: Sí, ganó el Madrid en Elche. Lo hizo pecando de nuevo, como en anteriores compromisos, cuajando un buen primer tiempo y coqueteando con el ridículo en el segundo. No mejora. Involuciona. Se fue 2-0 al descanso bajo la batuta de Arda, pero volvió de la pausa sin ambición, energía ni aplicación siquiera para defender, facilitando la reacción de un buen Elche, liderado por Osorio. No lo detectó Mourinho hasta que se vio 2-2 y entonces sí, recurrió a Espí. El recurso de toda la vida le dio resultado. Como en Cornellá. Habrá que ver qué ocurre en el Metropolitano. El primer relevo entre los intocables de la BMV no sentó mal al Madrid. Y no porque Bellingham estuviera flojo en partidos anteriores, no. De hecho, ha sido de lo mejor. Pero Arda Güler aprovechó la posición como enganche para mostrar su inspiración. Apareció en cada jugada de ataque, ofreciéndose, buscando pases de primera, al pie o al hueco, según conviniera a la jugada. Y lo del balón parado es indiscutible. Desde el córner, donde sirvió un caramelo para el cabezazo de Huijsen que le salió centrado, o desde la falta directa, donde abrió el marcador con un lanzamiento duro que entró tras tocar en el palo y en Dituro. La pelota corría paralela a la línea, y como no está demostrado que no fuera a entrar sin tocar al portero, pues se queda como acierto del lanzador. Mereció el Madrid ponerse por delante antes en el Martínez Valero, aunque el Elche salió respondón. Anselmi planteó un duelo más abierto buscando la profundidad de Morente y Valera más el remate de Osorio, pero chocó con los problemas en la salida de su equipo. En otro momento, o en otra temporada, Vinicius habría sumado al menos un par de tantos porque ocasiones tuvo para ello. Clamorosas. Empezó tras dejarle solo Arda en un pase fino. Siguió metiendo la puntera defectuosa, y acabó malgastando una cesión de Mbappé. Las tres, solo ante Dituro. Le falta finura. Al Elche le costó recobrarse del 0-1. Aunque buscó los costados para hacer daño, tuvo incluso suerte de no quedarse con diez si el VAR hubiera avisado a Gil Manzano de un codazo claro de Osorio a Huijsen. Por muchísimo menos vio amarilla en el primer lance Diomande, que empieza a entrar en dinámica. Se enfadó al no recibir alguna pelota en buena posición, y se apuntó una asistencia al entrar por derecha y servir un centro tenso para el remate de Mbappé. Siete en la cuenta. El francés quedó lastimado tras chocar con Dituro. Peor quedó su imagen al no querer mostrar, con Vinicius y Konaté, el mensaje previo con la camiseta de apoyo a Ceuta. Allá ellos. El 0-2 invitaba al Elche a no desengancharse por si el Madrid sesteaba como el día del Rayo. Diomande no buscó sólo su jugada. También se aplicó en tareas defensivas, lo cual es de agradecer. Pero lo cierto es que reincidieron los blancos con el ritmo cansino y el repliegue intensivo, a la espera de una contra que no llegaba. Equipo partido que permitió las llegadas del Elche, aunque sin obligar a Courtois. Anselmi refrescó la medular a la hora mientras Mourinho mandaba a los suyos a calentar, pero dilataba sus cambios, como es costumbre. El caso es que un partido que parecía bajo control se fue complicando hasta abrir la puerta a la ilusión franjiverde. Entraron Bellingham y Brahim por Güler, cansado, y Vinicius, desacertado. El brasileño había tirado fuera un mano a mano habilitado por el turco. Diomande se fue a la izquierda, pero no le dio tiempo a asomar. Lo hizo Cepeda por izquierda para ganar línea de fondo como los clásicos, poner un centro templadito y encontrar a un delantero de los de antes, Osorio, que se colgó del cielo para cabecear picado, perfecto. La empanada era monumental, y tampoco se hacía mucho desde el banquillo por despertar a la tropa. Así que pasó lo que tenía que pasar. Después de un puñado de balones perdidos absurdos, falló en la salida Cucurella, que no es sospechoso, gestionó bien el ataque por la derecha Lemar y Fer Niño, desde dentro del área, cruzó desde dentro del área ante el pasmo madridista. Ahí sí. Con el 2-2 ya salió Mourinho de la cueva y metió todos los delanteros posibles, Espí y Endrick, con cinco minutos por delante. Hasta cinco delanteros en busca de un milagro. Y lo encontró. Ya había avisado antes del 90 Espí con una media vuelta, porque es hombre de área. Pasado el tiempo, arrancó Bellingham por la izquierda, metió a Mbappé que pudo hacer el tanto pero vio a Espí en su sitio para completar el 2-3. Victoria que oculta un regreso evidente a los viejos vicios de un equipo con tendencia a haraganear. Si no se corrige, los títulos son imposibles.

articles.title: El recital de Arda no merecía este sofocón
articles.standfirst: 'En Copa de Balón', una opinión de Elías Israel
articles.summary: 'En Copa de Balón', una opinión de Elías Israel
articles.body: En vísperas del derbi del Metropolitano, la pasión turca se alimenta en el Real Madrid y los viejos vicios, también. Arda Güler ha cogido el tono, se le nota henchido de confianza y, cuando ese talento brota, al madridismo valora la variedad y la sutileza del elegido. Fue salir del campo y el Madrid empezó a sestear de una manera lamentable. Lo pudo pagar con dos puntos. Lo bueno: igual que en el bazar de Estambul te sirven un té y luego se negocia. Arda parece haber aprendido de ese protocolo; una pausa con el balón antes de soltarlo es oro. Esa pausa es justo lo que le falta a un Madrid que va a mil por hora. Por muy buenas que sean, y son extraordinarias, las flechas doradas que vuelan en ataque, Arda tiene la capacidad de tensar ese arco que da sentido al fútbol blanco. Un equipo que solo corre vende siempre lo mismo. Con Arda, el Madrid vuelve a tener surtido: la pausa, el pase de fuera, la conducción y el balón parado. Güler también tiene sus imperfecciones: seguramente podría mejorar algo su físico, su capacidad defensiva o la continuidad en el manejo del tempo de los partidos, pero en este Real Madrid es la esmeralda que da brillo a todo lo que le rodea. El equipo blanco, por comparación está muy necesitado de magia. La presencia de Tchouaméni le hace muy bien para liberar su calidad. Fue salir Arda del campo y el sesteo se hizo perceptible y reaparecieron los fantasmas de las dos Ligas anteriores. El problema es que los puntos de Elche valen lo mismo que los del Metropolitano. El Madrid no puede jugar con fuego de esa manera, aunque le acabe saliendo bien. Levantar el pie del acelerador de manera tan ostensible es una temeridad porque te pintan la cara como ocurrió. El Elche vendió cara su piel e hizo soñar a sus aficionados. Un destello de Bellingham, la generosidad de Mbappé y el oportunismo de Espí, el fichaje más rentable en lo que va de curso, evitó el incendio. El partidazo de Güler no merecía semejante sofoco. En el bazar de Arda se regatea hasta la felicidad.

articles.title: Mourinho: "Mi única crítica es que podemos matar los partidos y no lo hacemos"
articles.standfirst: La rueda de prensa del entrenador del Real Madrid tras el partido ante el Elche
articles.summary: La rueda de prensa del entrenador del Real Madrid tras el partido ante el Elche
articles.body: Jose Mourinho compareció ante la prensa aliviado por la victoria in extremis ante el Elche, aunque consciente de que su equipo jugó con fuego y que todavía hay muchas cosas que mejorar. Pero el luso sonríe por el triunfo. "Tres puntos nada más. Obviamente que después del primer tiempo la sensación era de 3, 4 ó 5 en el segundo tiempo. Bajamos la intensidad, dejamos mucho espacio... Intenté dar más consistencia en el centro del campo con Jude y Brahim... Pero justo ellos nos hicieron el 2-1 y en estos campos, con este ambientazo, el equipo que parece muerto se viene arriba", reflexionó. Los cambios del final: "Tenemos mucho talento. Y nosotros arriesgamos al máximo, con jugadores que tenían un sentimiento de que no podíamos perder... E hicimos unos últimos minutos muy buenos" Las rotaciones: "Hemos hecho cambios y Mbappé y Konaté son los únicos que han jugado completos los partidos de Inter, Rayo y Elche. La gente está unida, motivada, amistad, compromiso... Mi única crítica es que podemos matar los partidos y no lo hacemos y hemos dado la opción de dar vida a un equipo que parecía muerto". El derbi: "Habrá que descansar ahora y empezar a preparar el partido el jueves". Las desconexiones: "El problema me parece obvio... Hay partidos que parecen acabados que no están acabados. La única explicación que encuentro es que son partidos fáciles, no matas... Partidos que no matamos y parece que pasamos de la facilidad a no controlar. Este tipo de estadio, lleno, afición fantástica... Lo ponen difícil. La cosa buena es que con la dificultad, el equipo reacciona y gana, que es lo más importante. Y cosa buena es que con los partidos del Madrid nadie se aburre, porque son muy divertidos". Espí: "Lo está haciendo bien, es un chico con gran motivación. Tiene por delante a un jugador que no es normal y jugar con los dos juntos no es fácil, porque no tenemos por banda típicos jugadores para un 4-4-2. Al final hemos arriesgado todo porque el empate no sirve". Diomande: "Está creciendo. Tiene muy buena capacidad de trabajo, inteligencia, porque no es fácil jugar 85 minutos con una amarilla. Ha hecho un gran trabajo. Estoy contento". La defensa, encajando goles en cada partido: "Me gusta mucho que mi equipo marca goles, pero me gusta controlar los partidos, no me gusta regalar... Nos pueden meter un gol fuera de contexto, pero hoy llegaron porque perdimos el control del juego. Anselmi ha jugado muy bien, ha hecho buenos cambios, nos ha complicado la vida...". Güler: "No es imprescindible, nadie es imprescindible. Cuando hago los cambios es porque estábamos perdiendo el control. Arda estaba bajando su intensidad, porque jugaba en la posición de 10 y eso es abarcar todo el campo". Tchouaméni: "Cuando el equipo ha estado bien, ellos han estado muy bien. Hemos salido bien de la presión, con mucha calidad, pero nuestro partido tiene dos caras. O tres caras, mejor dicho. Porque al final ha sido de matamos o morimos".

articles.standfirst: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.summary: 'Al otro lado del espejo', una opinión de Alfredo Relaño
articles.body: Otra vez un gol de Espí en ‘la zona Cesarini’ para salvar al Madrid, cuyo partido en el Martínez Valero fue preocupante por el intenso sesteo de la segunda mitad. La primera fue, digamos, aceptable. Mourinho dejó descansar a Bellingham, le dio la manija a Güler, la banda derecha a Diomande, y el doble pivote a Valverde-Tchouaméni, la pareja del feo suceso del curso pasado. Funcionó, digamos, correctamente. Ante un Elche flojo para defender y malo para salir, el Madrid controló, creó ocasiones y marcó dos, que no fueron más porque Vinicius mandó al limbo un par de ocasiones claras. Diomande, que va entrando, le facilitó un gol a Mbappé tras perseguir un buen pase profundo de Valverde. El otro lo marcó Güler de golpe franco con un tiro colocadísimo al palo del portero, que la esperaba al otro lado. Pero la segunda parte del Madrid fue infame. Ganduleó, le dio al Elche el campo y el balón, y arriba ese equipo sí tiene cosas, sobre todo el delantero Osorio, que por cierto habría merecido la expulsión por un codazo a Huijsen que el árbitro no vio y el VAR dejó pasar porque la instrucción ahora es que entren poco. (Tantos vaivenes son desquiciantes). Así que marcó con toda justicia dos goles y Mourinho, que ya había hecho un par de cambios (retiró a Vinicius y mandó a Diomande a la izquierda, donde estuvo muy bien), sacó a Espí y Endrick. Con poco tiempo, pero el suficiente, el Madrid pegó el consabido apretón del vago y acabó por marcar, de nuevo por medio de Espí, ese nueve de buena planta y gran sentido del gol. Acompañó por el segundo palo la penetración de Mbappé por la izquierda y colocó con comodidad en la red el pase de este. Buen final para el Madrid, que en el prólogo tuvo un detalle feo. Los dos equipos salieron con una camiseta de solidaridad con Ceuta (“Todos somos caballas”), pero Konaté, Vinicius y Mbappé se la pusieron remangada, de manera que no se leía el mensaje, e incluso se la quitaron antes del saludo entre los dos equipos. Se distinguieron para mal en un asunto que conmociona a todo el país.

articles.title: Espí evita otro ridículo de Mourinho
articles.standfirst: La opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.summary: La opinión de José Vicente Hernáez
articles.body: Esta es la pregunta del millón: ¿qué narices le pasa al Madrid, a este Madrid, fuera de casa? Porque en el Bernabéu está goleando, aunque los segundos tiempos son para hacérselos mirar. Ya sucedió en Cornellá, contra el Espanyol. Era un partido que tenía que ganar el Madrid por lo civil (y no por lo criminal) y tuvo que ser Carlos Espí el que evitó en el último minuto que le pusieran la carita colorada a Mourinho. Después perdió en La Cartuja ante el Betis. Cierto que no mereció perder ese partido (incluso tuvo que ganarlo), pero el caso es que lo perdió. Y en esta ocasión estuvo a punto de pinchar otra vez cuando debió ganar al Elche por 0-4 como mínimo. De hecho, del posible 0-3 de Vinícius (Arda Güler hizo mal en pasarle el balón a él y no a Mbappé) se pasó al 1-2. Y no fue una casualidad. Se veía venir, porque el segundo tiempo del Madrid, tras irse 0-2 al descanso, fue infame, por decirlo sin la menor acritud. Un empate habría sido un ridículo tremendo. En Elche precisamente comenzó el descenso a los infiernos de Xabi Alonso la pasada temporada. Dejó a Vinícius de salida en el banquillo (entró en el minuto 57) y habría perdido el partido de no ser por el gol de Bellingham en el minuto 88, tras un pase de Mbappé, como sucedió en esta ocasión, curiosamente. En aquella ocasión se le comenzó a ir también el liderato al Madrid y en esta ocasión lo que comenzó a volar fue la confianza en Mourinho, del que no se explica que tome medidas para evitar el hundimiento del equipo en los segundos tiempos. Y es que no se concibe que este Madrid tenga problemas ante el Elche cuando otros le han goleado. Una lástima que el Madrid haya dejado este recuerdo cuando Yan Diomande causó una buena impresión. En fin, que el Madrid no ha inyectado ilusión en los madridistas ante la que se le avecina el domingo en el Metropolitano.

articles.title: Anselmi, pese a la derrota: "Si yo fuese hincha del Elche estaría orgulloso de mi equipo"
articles.standfirst: El técnico franjiverde lamenta el final ante el Real Madrid, pide madurez a sus jugadores y asegura que los resultados llegarán si mantienen el nivel de rendimiento
articles.summary: El técnico franjiverde lamenta el final ante el Real Madrid, pide madurez a sus jugadores y asegura que los resultados llegarán si mantienen el nivel de rendimiento
articles.body: Martín Anselmi terminó el partido ante el Real Madrid con una mezcla de enfado y orgullo. La derrota por 2-3 en el Martínez Valero volvió a dejar al Elche sin premio después de una remontada que permitió al conjunto franjiverde igualar un 0-2, pero el técnico argentino quiso poner el foco en la capacidad de su equipo para competir ante uno de los grandes de la competición. "Enfado es el sentimiento que tengo. Me saldría más orgullo por el juego y conseguirlo", reconoció Anselmi en sala de prensa. El entrenador consideró que al Elche le faltó gestionar mejor los últimos minutos: "No es fácil terminar este tipo de partidos. Nos faltó juntar lo que habíamos conseguido". Aun así, destacó la evolución mostrada por sus futbolistas y volvió a utilizar una palabra clave: madurez. "Me quedo con la palabra madurez, hemos madurado como hicimos en San Mamés", señaló. Para Anselmi, el equipo ha demostrado que puede competir ante cualquier adversario: "Elche es un equipo que sabe competir, hay jerarquía enfrente, pero consiguieron empatar y terminamos metiendo al Madrid aguantando en el córner". La derrota no ha cambiado la percepción del técnico sobre el potencial de su plantilla. "La imagen es que podemos contra el rival que sea. Hemos competido y los detalles no caen a nuestro favor", explicó. En este sentido, considera que este tipo de encuentros deben servir de aprendizaje para evitar repetir errores en el futuro. Anselmi también quiso destacar la unión con la afición. "Tenía ganas de acercarme porque siempre están. Estamos cerca de darles una alegría", afirmó. Y lanzó un mensaje a los seguidores: "Si yo fuese hincha del Elche estaría orgulloso de mi equipo". Pese a la situación clasificatoria y a las derrotas acumuladas, el entrenador no se mostró preocupado por el hecho de ser colista. "Me tengo que basar en el rendimiento y así pronto los resultados van a llegar", aseguró.

articles.title: Ed Sheeran blames US tour promoter for dropping Macklemore
articles.summary: The British musician said it was important to “set out some facts” after US rapper voiced support for Palestine.
articles.body:
Pop star Ed Sheeran has blamed the promoter of his United States tour for dropping Macklemore after the rapper voiced support for Palestine.

In a series of six slides on an Instagram post, Sheeran on Tuesday said it was important to “set out some facts”.

The decision to remove Macklemore from the US Loop Tour, Sheeran said, came after venues said they would pull future shows if they included Macklemore. The rapper, whose real name is Ben Haggerty, drew criticism after making “Free Palestine” and other pro-Palestine comments while on tour with Sheeran at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey earlier this month.

“I was informed that this stance was based on how Macklemore conveyed part of this message during his performance, rather than on everything that was said,” Sheeran wrote. “I spoke with the venues at length all week to try and build a bridge.”

Some musical artists, including supporting acts, said later on Tuesday that they were quitting Sheeran’s tour after Macklemore’s ouster. They included Irish singer-songwriter Aaron Rowe, Irish band Beoga, Danish band Lukas Graham and musician Finneas. They voiced support for Macklemore and expressed solidarity with Palestinians.

Robert Kraft, the owner of the National Football League’s New England Patriots, confirmed he pressured Sheeran to drop Macklemore from the tour. The billionaire said Macklemore was barred from appearing at the team’s Gillette Stadium in Massachusetts during a performance later this month due to what he described as a “broader history of antisemitic rhetoric and imagery”.

In an Instagram post, Macklemore said Sheeran told him Kraft had organised a boycott among other stadium owners unless he was thrown off the tour for his pro-Palestine remarks.

“I told him that if those words were more offensive than the tens of thousands of Palestinian children being killed by Israel, then there was a fundamental disconnect between where those people stood and where I stood,” Macklemore said of his conversation with Sheeran.

Sheeran said the decision to boot Macklemore off the tour was the promoter’s, not his. The British musician added that he was “appalled by the conflict between Israel and Palestine”.

“I am not complicit. I have my personal views on the devastating conflict. Just because I choose not to speak publicly, it doesn’t mean I don’t have them, and it doesn’t mean I don’t care. Nor does it mean I don’t support causes in my own, personal way,” Sheeran said.

Kraft, in a statement to Al Jazeera, said the decision to ban Macklemore from his venue wasn’t about “diminishing the suffering of innocent Palestinians” but argued “advocacy should not come at the expense of the Jewish community or obscure the responsibility of Hamas”.

Macklemore, who described Sheeran as a close friend, said the two artists had discussed the issue over the past week.

“He couldn’t get past his public-facing, ‘I don’t take sides,’” Macklemore wrote, referring to Sheeran’s reluctance to take a public stance on Israel’s war on Gaza.

Sheeran explained why he doesn’t use his “professional platform for politics”, writing that audiences who attend his shows “do not expect a political forum”.

“I respect Macklemore’s strength of purpose to stand up and shout for what he believes,” Sheeran said. “However, there is room for multiple approaches to the same end: peace. I choose to use my fame and platform to be a place of safety and sanctuary, to maintain diplomacy and keep conversations open, not closed.”

images.caption: Ed Sheeran (right) said unlike Macklemore (left), he hasn't spoken publicly about Israel's war on Gaza but said 'it doesn't mean I don't care' [File: AP Photo]

articles.title: Max Dowman: Arsenal youngster shows his class - but Gunners wary of rushing him
articles.summary: Max Dowman shines with two goals against Ipswich Town - but boss Mikel Arteta warns Arsenal cannot rush his development.
articles.body:
Arsenal teenager Max Dowman shone with two goals in the 4-2 Carabao Cup win over Ipswich Town - but boss Mikel Arteta warned they cannot rush his development.

The 16-year-old played 13 times last season, but has had to settle for a place on the bench so far this campaign - until now.

He scored two lovely goals at Portman Road to stake his claim for more minutes in the Premier League.

But Arteta warned: "He is 16 years old and we have to be really cautious.

"We don't want to stop him, we don't want to put the brakes on him, we need to develop him and we are fully aware what he needs. He will have opportunities."

His first was a fine solo goal as he ran through, leaving defenders on the floor before slotting in.

"Unbelievable, he's unpredictable, he can go either way, so fluid, so nice to watch," said Arteta.

And for his second goal, Dowman showed good composure to place the ball in the bottom corner.

He is just the second 16-year-old to score two goals in a game for a Premier League side in any competition, after Wayne Rooney for Everton against Wrexham in 2002 - which was also in the League Cup.

"With the demands that we put in them, to be able to do that is extremely difficult and he's coping better and better and better," Arteta added.

"He's an unbelievable player because of the character that he has and how much he loves to play at the biggest stage.

"It's not easy [to contain the hype], I understand, but what we have to do is look after him. He's 16 years old. You don't see that in this league.

"In other leagues in Europe, that's a totally different context, but in this league, with the demands that the league has, the players and everything put on you, we really need to make sure every time we throw him in, he's in the right context with the right preparation."

Perhaps Dowman might have expected to have more minutes this season.

His breakthrough came last season as he broke several records.

He became the youngest Champions League player ever, aged 15, Arsenal 's youngest ever starter as well as the Premier League's youngest starter, goalscorer and title winner.

In 13 appearances in all competitions, he scored once - against Everton to make a win safe during the title run-in.

In fact his strike, where he ran the ball halfway down the pitch before scoring into an empty net - with Jordan Pickford upfield - was voted Arsenal 's goal of the season.

And all of this while he was studying for school exams.

He received his GCSEs from Brentwood School in the summer and left school to focus on his football career.

Sky Sports pundit Jamie Redknapp said: "He is a wonderful player who will be able to do everything in the game.

"But just give him time and how they are handling him is perfect. What you don't want to do is not give him the amount of game time he needs. He is an elite player."

Breaking into the Arsenal first team will be a tough task for Dowman especially when the Premier League champions are in such fine form.

Arsenal have won all seven games this season, across four competitions.

Dowman was an unused substitute in four of those games, and not involved for the other two, before playing all 90 minutes against Ipswich Town .

The Gunners have played the same attackers in each league game so far - Bukayo Saka, Christos Tzolis, Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz.

But Dowman, especially considering Arteta turned to him in key moments in last season's title race, will hope to gain more of a supporting role.

"He's an unbelievable talent," team-mate Mikel Merino told BBC Radio 5 Live.

"He will be a star in the future if he keeps his eyes and ears open and keeps learning.

"He's just 16 so he needs a lot of coaching, especially tactically. But I can't take anything away from him. He's always keen to learn. We'll keep helping him."

Quite possibly the best 16-year-old in the world, it is not unthinkable that he could earn his way into England's Euro 2028 thinking.

In fact there was even a debate about whether he should be going to the World Cup earlier this year.

"He is a real superstar," said former England defender Conor Coady on Sky Sports.

"A 16-year-old boy should not be doing this. He has got no better manager than Arteta to look after him. You want him to be looked after properly. If he plays every game at this age, he won't be scoring goals like this."

And it comes on the day it emerged highly rated 15-year-old striker JJ Gabriel is on the verge of leaving Manchester United.

Gabriel had been expected to make his debut in Wednesday's Carabao Cup tie with Brighton .

That will probably deny him the opportunity to break up the stat that the three youngest players to score in the League Cup for a Premier League side all did so for Arsenal .

They are Cesc Fabregas (16y 212d v Wolves, 2003), Dowman (16y 258d v Ipswich) and Jack Wilshere (16y 266d v Sheffield United, 2008).

articles.title: Vinicius entona el 'mea culpa': "Los goles van a volver, no puedo fallar tantas"
articles.standfirst: El brasileño se pronunció en sus redes sociales al final del partido
articles.summary: El brasileño se pronunció en sus redes sociales al final del partido
articles.body: Vinicius Junior tampoco encontró el gol en Elche. El brasileño lo buscó de todas las maneras, pero volvió a mostrar una falta de puntería desesperante hasta para sus propios compañeros, que se llevaban las manos a la cabeza en el banquillo. Hasta Mou se lo reclamaba en la previa: "Le falta el gol". Y Vini lo sabe, hasta el punto de que entonó el mea culpa en sus redes sociales al final del encuentro. "Los goles van a volver, no puedo fallar tanto...". Vinicius anda con la pólvora mojada esta temporada, en la que solo suma un gol en las primeras seis jornadas. Ante el Elche tuvo dos clarísimas, pero en ambas ocasiones definió mal. En la primera, solo con Dituro, utilizó la puntera y mandó el balón muy desviado de la portería. En esa acción le pedía el balón Arda, pero se la jugó Vini, que tenía buena posición, pero que no acertó. En la segunda parte dispuso de otra buena ocasión, pero otra vez su disparo se fue desviado. Fue Güler el que le dio un gran pase en una buena transición, pero siguió negado el brasileño, que fue sustituido a falta de media hora. Le vio cansado Mourinho y empezó a pensar en el derbi del domingo ante el Atlético. Mourinho felicitó a Vini por su esfuerzo, pero el brasileño siguió con su sequía, en un diagnóstico que ya había hecho el entrenador en la previa: "La mejor versión es marcar. Asistir es importante, trabajar para el equipo es muy importante, el trabajo del día es importante y lo hace muy bien... Pero existe otro Vinicius. Un Vinicius que llegó a Benfica el año pasado y que tiene una oportunidad, un gol y para casa. Le está faltando este performance de altísimo nivel". Ante el Atlético, una nueva oportunidad para Vini.

articles.title: Arch Manning, Texas' Win vs. OSU Sets Viewership Records, How Many Fans Watched Epic CFB Matchup?
articles.summary: A total of 14 million viewers (with a peak of 16.3 million viewers) watched Texas football's 24-23 comeback win over Ohio State last Saturday evening.
articles.body:
A total of 14 million viewers (with a peak of 16.3 million viewers) watched Texas football's 24-23 comeback win over Ohio State last Saturday evening.

It was ESPN's most-watched regular season college football game since Ohio State beat Michigan 30-27 in double overtime on Nov. 26, 2016.

It was the most-watched regular season primetime game on any network since 2012.

Quarterback Arch Manning and the Longhorns were down 23-3 entering the fourth quarter, but they scored three touchdowns in the final 14-plus minutes. Manning found Ryan Wingo for a three-yard pass, and Hollywood Smothers scored on a pair of one-yard runs. The second one happened with 25 seconds remaining.

Texas, which was fourth in the polls, heading into the evening, moved up to No. 1. Ohio State, the country's previously top-ranked team, fell to No. 6.

It's certainly possible these two teams meet again in the College Football Playoff for another potentially electric game that would attract millions of viewers.

In the meantime, Ohio State will look to bounce back Saturday afternoon at home vs. Kent State. Texas will host UTSA on Saturday evening.

articles.title: ESPN says Texas' win over Ohio State was its most-watched regular-season game in a decade
articles.summary: The Longhorns scored 21 straight points in the fourth quarter for the win.
articles.body:
No. 1 Texas ' comeback win over No. 6 Ohio State unsurprisingly drew a big audience on Saturday night. But that audience wasn't as big as it was in 2025.

ESPN said Tuesday that an average audience of 14 million people watched the Longhorns score 21 unanswered points in the fourth quarter of their 24-23 win. Ohio State was up 23-3 before Texas went on three touchdown drives that totaled 40 plays.

The network also said that it was ABC's biggest viewership number for a regular-season game in 10 years. In 2016, when ESPN still had the rights to the Big Ten, Ohio State's rivalry game with Michigan drew over 16.8 million viewers.

Last season, Texas and Ohio State played each other in Week 1. That game, at noon ET on Fox, drew an average audience of 16.6 million. The game was Arch Manning 's first as Texas' undisputed starter, and he entered the season as the Heisman favorite despite playing part-time in 2024.

Ohio State's 14-7 win in 2025 ended up being the second-most watched game of the regular season behind, you guessed it, Ohio State's win over Michigan. That game drew 18.4 million viewers.

ABC's most-watched regular season game in 2025 was Texas' win over Texas A&M on Black Friday. The Longhorns' win to end the Aggies' hopes of making the SEC championship game drew an average audience of just over 13 million.

ESPN and ABC also immediately have a chance to rival the Texas-Ohio State viewership number in Week 3. ABC's primetime game on Saturday is No. 7 LSU at No. 8 Ole Miss as former Rebels coach Lane Kiffin returns to Oxford following his tumultuous exit ahead of last season's College Football Playoff.

articles.title: Lionel Messi named in Argentina squad for farewell friendly against Benin
articles.summary: Argentina name Lionel Messi in their squad for a friendly against Benin in October in a match which is set to be the forward's farewell to international football.
articles.body:
Argentina have named Lionel Messi in their squad for a friendly against Benin in October in a match which is set to be the forward's farewell to international football.

Messi announced his retirement from Argentina duty in August in the wake of his country's defeat by Spain in the 2026 World Cup final and after saying he was considering his future in football following the death of his father, Jorge.

The 39-year-old, who captained Argentina when they won the 2022 World Cup, said the decision to stop playing for La Albiceleste hurt him "deeply" but that he had "given it my all" and had "nothing left to give".

Messi, an eight-time Ballon d'Or winner who currently plays for Inter Miami, is Argentina's all-time leading scorer and most-capped player, having scored 125 goals in 207 appearances.

"We made the decision to invite the best player in the world, the symbol of our national team, our captain, Lionel Andres Messi, so that he can have the farewell he truly deserves on 6 October here in Argentina," said Argentine FA president Claudio Tapia.

River Plate's Estadio Monumental in Buenos Aires, which has an 85,000 capacity, will host the game against Benin.

Argentina's 2022 World Cup winners have also been invited to the match, which Tapia said would be an "unforgettable" occasion.

Messi retires from Argentina duty with 'nothing left to give'

Messi unsure he will play 'much longer' after father's death

Argentina were ordered to play their next two home matches with 50% capacity, although one match of that sanction was suspended, for breaches of the Fifa disciplinary code during the World Cup.

The punishment related to using a sports event for demonstrations of a non-sporting nature, team misconduct, and discriminatory chants and gestures by its supporters.

After defeating England 2-1 in the World Cup semi-final, several Argentina players held up a banner claiming Argentine sovereignty over the Falkland Islands, a British overseas territory.

As they play friendlies against Bolivia on 30 September in Cordoba and Burkina Faso in Buenos Aires on 3 October, it should mean the punishment will have been served before the Benin game.

Argentina midfielder Leandro Paredes and team-mate Nahuel Molina are not expected to be available as they were given respective 10-game and seven-match suspensions for their part in on-field clashes following their country's defeat by Spain in the World Cup final.

articles.title: EFL Cup - Reading 1-2 Brentford: Keith Andrews says VAR is stopping referees making decisions
articles.summary: After Brentford overcame Reading to reach the Carabao Cup fourth round, head coach Keith Andrews believes the video assistant referee (VAR) is preventing referees from making decisions in matches.
articles.body:
Brentford head coach Keith Andrews believes the video assistant referee (VAR) is preventing referees from making decisions in matches.

As his Bees progressed to the Carabao Cup fourth round with a battling 2-1 win at League One side Reading , Andrews said he was not happy with the officiating.

Reading defender Paudie O'Connor had a goal for a first-half overhead kick ruled out by referee Tom Nield for a high boot, prompting Royals boss Leam Richardson to say it was "possibly in the top three [wrong] decisions that I've seen in my career - and I've seen thousands of games and played in hundreds".

With no VAR used at this stage of the EFL Cup, Andrews added: "It's been a tough week for officials as everybody is probably aware.

"I think we just need to let them ref the game and be human beings and make decisions.

"We have gone through a period in the game where I feel like they weren't actually making decisions in both boxes because of the technology we have in the game and I feel like that is a real shame."

His comments followed the admission of Pro Ref to an "error of judgement" in awarding Erling Haaland's winning goal for Manchester City in their Premier League encounter at Manchester United on Sunday.

There was intense debate over whether the goal should have been disallowed for City midfielder Enzo Fernandez - who was in an offside position - interfering with play as he dived, attempting to head the ball in a central position before Haaland's finish.

Andrews, whose Brentford side are seventh in the Premier League, said referees were no longer allowed to "make mistakes".

"I always felt as a player, when there was a relationship with an official that was built on respect and being able to speak to each other in a certain way," he added.

"We've gone away from allowing them to officiate and allowing them to make mistakes and I think it is a real shame.

"Now they are having to go back to that and it's not the habits they have had in recent years."

On Sunday's refereeing error in the Manchester derby, Andrews said it was "pretty alarming" Haaland's goal was allowed to stand.

"The first thing was whether [Erling] Haaland was offside and then obviously [Enzo] Fernandez was. It's a shame," he admitted.
